question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2x-y}, & \,x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ for $x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }2{e}^{-2x-y}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{e}^{-y}{lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{b}{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{e}^{-y}{lim}_{b\to \infty }(-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2}){|}_{0}^{b} \\  & ={e}^{-y}{lim}_{b\to \infty }(1-{e}^{-2b}) \\  & ={e}^{-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-y}, & \,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{-2x-y}}{{e}^{-y}} \\  & =2{e}^{-2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2x}, & \,x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
